findings.title: Mobile header still taller than target mock
findings.detail: Measured headerHeight on light-375 is 127px while mockup.headerHeight375 is 452 — wait, re-read: mockup has headerHeight375: 452 which seems like a large mock; frames report headerHeight: 127. More critically, firstTimelineCellVisible is false on all frames including light-375, so the first timeline cell is not above the fold despite header reductions. That may be intentional depending on design, but the measurement records a clear product defect vs fold goals if the goal was first cell visible.

findings.title: Touch targets fail WCAG/mobile sizing
findings.detail: Every frame records multiple touchFails for anchor tags with h: 21 (well under the 44px minimum). On mobile frames these are unlabeled links; on desktop frames include testid source-link at h:21 w:349. Shipping evidence that documents systematic sub-44px touch targets is a verified FAIL for mobile UX, not a green measurement.

findings.title: paint null on primary viewports
findings.detail: light-375, dark-375, light-1280, dark-1280, and light-375-drawer-open all have paint: null. Only paint-1440 (and presumably paint-1920) capture paint ratio. Theme/paint verification for the main responsive breakpoints is therefore not evidenced in this measure file despite screenshots being referenced.

findings.title: LIKE search order may return wrong zone
findings.detail: resolveZone name path uses WHERE name LIKE '%q%' ORDER BY name COLLATE NOCASE LIMIT 1. A short fragment can match multiple cities and silently returns the alphabetically first match rather than the best or unique match. Callers treating this as a precise lookup can get the wrong zone with no disambiguation error.

findings.title: AZ state filter is brittle string match
findings.detail: listZones special-cases token az/arizona with hardcoded LIKE patterns on name ('% AZ %', '% AZ(%', etc.). Zones named without that exact spacing/token (or only county/zip) are excluded; non-AZ names containing 'Arizona' substring would be included. This is fragile domain logic with no verification path in this chunk.

findings.title: feature-audit crawl may miss or mis-key controls
findings.detail: The added feature-audit crawler keys controls by data-testid or first class token or accessible name. Class-token keys are unstable under CSS modules/Tailwind and can produce false unclaimed/stale failures or silent mis-claims. Without a manifest or test run output in this chunk, correctness of PASS/FAIL behavior for this app is not verified.

findings.title: Touch-target check uses 40px floor, not 44px
findings.detail: Touch-target probe gates on r.height < 40 after already checking r.height < 44, so controls between 40–43px tall (and any control with height ≥40 but width <44) are never reported. WCAG 2.5.5 / mobile touch guidance is typically 44×44 CSS px. This measurement script will green-light undersized targets that fail the product standard the script claims to measure.

findings.title: Theme applied after networkidle without viewport set
findings.detail: measure() accepts width/height but never calls page.setViewportSize({ width, height }). All runs therefore measure at Chromium’s default viewport while reporting width/height in the JSON (375, 1280, 1440, 1920). Layout metrics (searchY, brandMarkH, paintedPct, truncation, screenshots named home-${theme}-${width}.png) are not valid for those viewports. FAIL: metrics cannot be trusted as multi-viewport evidence.

findings.title: Hardcoded waitForTimeout for theme settle
findings.detail: await page.waitForTimeout(250) after forcing data-theme. Fixed sleeps are not a ready signal; theme/CSS paint can lag or race. Combined with missing viewport sizing, this weakens the measurement as proof of light/dark correctness.

findings.title: paintCoverage treats any non-transparent bg as painted
findings.detail: Sampled points count as painted if backgroundColor is not transparent OR if the element has text color + textContent. A wrong theme (e.g. dark hero on light page) still counts as painted. This cannot fail a hardcoded/theme-mismatch paint defect and therefore is not a meaningful coverage gate.

findings.title: Truncation probe skips intentional ellipsis classes inconsistently
findings.detail: Header-build skips live-search__label, theme-toggle__sr-only, skip-link; chosen-design truncation does not. Different scripts can disagree on truncatedCount for the same UI. Not a product bug by itself, but measurement disagreement means neither count alone proves zero truncation.

findings.title: CSP measurement confuses console noise with policy enforcement
findings.detail: CSP “violations” are scraped from console text matching /Content Security Policy|CSP|Refused to apply inline style/i, then cspHeader is read from fetch headers with a fallback string claiming public/_headers. Console regex can false-positive; absence of console matches does not prove CSP is correct or deployed. Report also embeds public/_headers file contents as evidence without verifying the live edge applies them.

findings.title: API success not checked before .json() / reduce
findings.detail: zoneRes/cropsRes/zonesRes are fetched without checking res.ok. crops.crops.reduce assumes shape { crops: [...] }; a 500 HTML body or error JSON throws and aborts the report after browser work completed. Fragile measurement pipeline; failure mode is crash, not a structured fail.

findings.title: searchCountY only collected for two widths that were never set
findings.detail: if (width === 375 || width === 1280) fills search and records searchCountY, but viewport is never resized to those widths. The tomato search path still runs under default viewport for every loop iteration’s width parameter, so searchCountY is not a 375/1280 metric.

findings.title: navClass signature mismatch with PrimaryNavLinks
findings.detail: Layout passes className={navClass} to PrimaryNavLinks after changing navClass from ({ isActive }) => string to (isActive: boolean) => string. React Router NavLink className receives { isActive, isPending, isTransitioning }, not a bare boolean. If PrimaryNavLinks forwards the prop to NavLink as className={className}, navClass will receive an object, which is always truthy, so every link permanently gets topbar__link--active. If PrimaryNavLinks calls className(isActive) with a boolean this works — but that contract is not visible in this chunk, and the rename of the parameter type without an adapter is a high-risk API break at the call site shown.

findings.title: Home omits chrome that non-home pages get
findings.detail: When isHome, Layout renders no topbar, no Breadcrumbs, and no AssistantPanel dock. Comment claims Home uses CompactHeader inside HomePage, but this chunk does not show HomePage providing equivalent primary nav, zone selector, theme toggle, skip-target parity, or assistant access. Footer remains, but global controls (theme, zone, nav menu) are absent from the Layout shell on `/`. Fail closed: home chrome parity is not verified in this patch.

findings.title: Footer plantable link is hard navigation hash
findings.detail: Uses <a href="/#plantable-now"> instead of React Router Link. That forces a full document navigation when already on the SPA, and on non-home routes it leaves the current route entirely. Also has no SPA scroll/hash handling guarantee for #plantable-now after client-side loads. Prefer Link to="/#plantable-now" or a documented in-app scroll target.

findings.title: useTheme cycle still depends on readThemeMode/applyThemeMode
findings.detail: cycle() now reads storage then calls applyThemeMode(next) and setModeState(next). The comment about stale React state is sound, but this chunk does not show that applyThemeMode and readThemeMode stay consistent with the [mode] effect path, or that setMode (if still exported) applies the same eager path. Cannot verify the full theme toggle contract from the partial hunk alone beyond the cycle body shown.

findings.title: ZoneProvider overwrites selection whenever zonesPayload changes
findings.detail: useEffect depends only on [zonesPayload] and always setZoneState(preferred) from localStorage/default. On reload() after the user has selected a different zone in-session, if zonesPayload is a new object reference with the same list, the effect re-runs and re-applies stored id — correct if setZone wrote storage first. But if setZone failed to write (private mode catch is empty), reload will snap back to DEFAULT_ZONE_ID / first zone, discarding the session selection. Also, when storedId is missing/invalid, always falls to DEFAULT_ZONE_ID without user confirmation.

findings.title: LegalPage keys list items by full text
findings.detail: li key={item} and section key={section.heading} will collide or remount poorly if two sections share a heading or two bullets share text. Minor React stability issue; content structure is otherwise fine as a presentational shell — substance of legal copy is not in this file.

findings.title: LiveSearch CSS incomplete in judge view
findings.detail: File is new (222+ lines claimed) but the supplied chunk truncates mid-rule at .live-search__item. Styles that are present use theme tokens (var(--surface), var(--text), var(--accent)) correctly — no hardcoded light/dark paint in the visible portion. Remaining rules and the LiveSearch.tsx behavior are not fully present in the message body after truncation; only token usage in the visible CSS can be noted, not full component correctness.

findings.title: unparseable judge output
findings.detail: chunk 7/8 did not return JSON — cannot verify; fail closed

findings.title: isDarkRgb hand-parses CSS colors
findings.detail: Theme light/dark proof uses a hand-rolled rgba() regex + luma threshold on getComputedStyle backgroundColor. That fails closed for non-rgb forms (hex, color(), color-mix, oklab) and is the known false-pass/false-fail pattern the project rules ban in favor of axe-core or real paint checks. The screenshot paths are written but this chunk only shows the heuristic gate; if production CSS ever emits non-rgb(), the theme assertion silently returns false and the expect can pass or fail without measuring real paint.

findings.title: forceThemeMode can miss target mode
findings.detail: forceThemeMode clicks the toggle at most 4 times, then asserts data-theme-mode equals the target. With nextThemeMode skipping indistinguishable steps, the cycle length is not fixed at 3 presses from an arbitrary start; four clicks is usually enough, but the helper never waits for storage/DOM settle between clicks and only checks the attribute after the loop. A flaky intermediate attribute or a skip that lands on an unexpected intermediate can make the final expect fail without proving the theme pipeline is broken — or pass if the attribute is updated before paint. This is a weak ready-signal for a theme test that claims to verify real dark/light hero backgrounds.

findings.title: API 404 acceptance test not verifiable from this patch alone for middleware fix
findings.detail: The new test correctly requires unmatched /api/* to return 404 JSON with error containing 'no such endpoint', and real routes to stay 200 JSON. That is a good regression harness for the SPA-fallback bug described in the comment. This chunk does not include the middleware/functions implementation that implements that 404; the test documents expected behavior but success of the product fix is not proven by the test file alone in this patch. The test itself is well-formed; no defect in the test design.

findings.title: Theme default and cycle logic look correct with unit coverage
findings.detail: STORAGE_KEY renamed to 'theme', default mode changed from 'system' to 'light', and nextThemeMode skips candidates whose resolveTheme equals the current resolved appearance. theme.test.ts covers cycle under OS light/dark, persistence of light/dark/system, and the no-identical-step regression. Unit coverage for the pure logic is solid.

findings.title: Vitest coverage include excludes UI components by design
findings.detail: Coverage is limited to src/lib/**, src/theme.ts, and functions/** with an explicit rationale that components are Playwright surface. That is coherent; not a defect.

findings.title: Wrangler AI binding added without usage in this chunk
findings.detail: [ai] binding = "AI" is added. This chunk shows no Workers code consuming env.AI, no secrets/docs, and no tests for AI. Binding alone is harmless if unused, but it is an unproven dependency surface: if production code in other chunks assumes AI without handling missing binding in local/dev, that would fail elsewhere. No explicit misuse visible here.

findings.title: Acceptance hero viewport ratio weakened
findings.detail: Hero visibility check changed from default in-viewport to scrollIntoViewIfNeeded + toBeInViewport({ ratio: 0.01 }). A 1% intersection still passes if almost all of the hero is off-screen after 'scroll into view', so the assertion no longer proves the hero is meaningfully in the first viewport as product UX. That looks like a test softened to match a layout where the timeline is the true first-viewport hero (which the comment states). Acceptable if product intent is timeline-first; weak if the claim is still 'plantable hero is above the fold'.

findings.title: Tailwind v4 vite plugin wired
findings.detail: Adds @tailwindcss/vite plugin. Diff does not show package.json dependency change in this chunk; if the package is missing, build breaks. Incomplete verification of install wiring from this patch alone, but the config change itself is the correct Vite 6 / Tailwind v4 pattern.
